messages:
Emma: Quick heads-up: found a reproducible correctness + perf regression in the fp8 fused/paged flash kernel when KV cache is warm and seq length > 1536. After ~150-300 tokens some batches start returning near-zero logits and throughput drops ~10-13%

Raj: Which hardware/drivers and a minimal repro please?

Emma: Repro on rtx-a6000, driver 535.101, pytorch nightly. Short bench:
```
python -m perf.attn_bench --model=tiny --seq=2048 --kv-cache=warm --kernel=flash_fp8_fused
Throughput: 471 tok/s (expected ~530)
```
nvprof summary:
```
flash_fp8_fused: 79.6ms, softmax_exp: 41.2ms, tiled_reduction: 19.8ms, fallback_kernel: 6.4ms
```

Lisa: I pulled micro-traces of the tiled softmax across rows. The exponentials grow to ~1e8-1e9 before exp -> clamp/underflow and you get effectively zeroed probabilities. Looks like some tiled path skips the row-wise max-subtract step.

Tom: That would explain both correctness and perf (exp costs + denorm handling). Is it specific to paged/tiled fused path or all fused variants?

Emma: Narrowed it down: non-paged flash_fp8_fused is stable. The issue triggers when paged attention is used and KV cache is hot/compacted — i.e., when we reuse buffer slices across tiles.

Anna: I inspected cache compaction code. We're reusing buffer slices and not clearing per-tile scaling/metadata flags. If a previous tile used a different exponent/precision path the fused kernel can assume normalization already happened. So two things collide: stale metadata + fast-path that omits subtract-max.

Raj: Can you point to the kernel area? A defensive quick fix is to always do a max-subtract in the tiled softmax before exp, using fp32 accumulators, e.g.:
```
// softmax_fused_tiled_fp8.cu (concept)
float maxv = -INFINITY;
for (int j=0;j<N;j++) maxv = fmaxf(maxv, (float)x[j]);
for (int j=0;j<N;j++) out[j] = expf((float)x[j] - maxv);
// accumulate and normalize in fp32
```
That trades a few ops for safety.

Lisa: Microbenchmark: flipping on "always_subtract_max" restores correct outputs for seq=2048 cold/warm KV, but long-seq throughput drops ~3-5%. Correctness regained is higher priority though.

Tom: Alternative: implement a heuristic guarded path. Fast-path (no subtract) for seq < 1024 or cold cache; guarded-softmax when kv_cache_size > threshold OR when tiled reduction detects high variance / large dynamic range. That should keep most traffic fast.

Emma: Also want better telemetry: add kernel-selector metrics that emit softmax_exp latency distribution and fallback_kernel ratio to Console. If we alert on >2x baseline softmax_exp or fallback rate >1% we can catch regressions early.

Anna: I'll open a PR with two changes: (1) clear scaling metadata during cache compaction (safe no-regress), (2) guarded-softmax toggle + kernel-selector heuristic + unit tests (seq=2048 cold/warm and a short perf-smoke).

ci-bot: build queued for PR #4851 — running attn-unit, perf-smoke, bench-matrix

Raj: After merge let's run a HW matrix (a6000, h100, t4, v100) and check fp8/bf16/fp16/fp32. BF16/FP16 have smaller exponent range so we should validate those too.

Lisa: I'll run the sweep and post CSVs to #bench. Current pre-fix baseline snapshot I measured locally: flash_fp32=540 tok/s, flash_bf16=522, flash_fp16=499, flash_fp8_fused=471 (problematic at long seqs).

Emma: Thanks. Priority order: correctness first, then recover perf via heuristic switchover + kernel-selection telemetry. Also add per-customer "aggressive_fast_path" opt-in flag for Dedicated customers who prefer throughput over robustness.

Tom: I'll prototype the selector metric + console alert (fallback_rate > 1% or softmax_exp P95 > 2x baseline).

(edited)
